correctness.rationale: Exactly 70 odd primes p<=353 enumerated by complete sieve. Algebraic equivalence of tuple condition and clique graph is exact. The included bitset branch-and-bound proof uses proper color classes as certified clique upper bounds and partitions branches exhaustively; all witnesses directly checked. This is a finite exhaustive proof, not extrapolation. Ten record primes independently cross-checked via separate enumerator.

originality.rationale: The complete prime-field first-occurrence spectrum through size 12 and M(353)=12 were not derived in inspected primary papers. Published exact counts stop at smaller tuple orders; general existence/asymptotic estimates do not settle the sharp finite prime minima or the exclusions. Actual semantic and exact-sequence searches uncovered no equivalent table, though absence from indexes does not prove novelty.
residual_risks: Some earlier tables or programs not indexed by the searched literature could have obtained these exact prime thresholds.
Only the prime-field finite cutoff through 353 is proved; wider prime powers or arbitrary m are not covered.
The older preprint already supplies small-m existence information; the strongest distinctive new data start at m=7.

value.rationale: First-occurrence primes P(m) are natural sharp arithmetic field-size invariants complementing the 2021 published question asking how large p must be for existence. The full spectrum through m=12 resolves precise first occurrences rather than arbitrary slices. It provides witnesses and complete exclusion certificates for finite-field construction tests; no infinite generality or downstream theorem is asserted.
